panels.title: Cluster CPU
panels.description:
Amber at 85%, red at 95% (sustained), as VME's Host/VM CPU Usage alarms. Short peaks are normal.

Colours match VME's default HVM alarm thresholds ([HVM alarms](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/alarms.rst)).

panels.title: N+1 failover headroom: VM memory vs capacity left if a host fails
panels.description:
Memory allocated to running VMs, as a share of what the cluster could still hold if its largest host failed.
Each host keeps 4 GB for itself (OS, cluster services, agent, libvirt). VME treats VM memory as a reservation
(no memory overcommit by default), so **over 100% means a host failure or maintenance evacuation can't place every VM**.
HPE's rule: never allocate more than (N-1)/N of cluster memory, e.g. keep 33% free on 3 hosts
([capacity planning](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/capacity_planning.rst)).

targets.rawSql: WITH h AS (SELECT cluster_id, id, max_memory - 4294967296 AS usable FROM servers WHERE kind = 'host' AND present AND cluster_id IS NOT NULL), c AS (SELECT cluster_id, count(*) AS hosts, sum(usable) AS usable, sum(usable) - max(usable) AS n1 FROM h GROUP BY 1), v AS (SELECT h.cluster_id, sum(vm.max_memory) AS alloc FROM servers vm JOIN h ON h.id = vm.host_id WHERE vm.kind = 'vm' AND vm.present AND vm.power_state = 'on' GROUP BY 1) SELECT cl.name, 100.0 * COALESCE(v.alloc, 0) / NULLIF(c.n1, 0) AS pct FROM c JOIN clusters cl ON cl.id = c.cluster_id LEFT JOIN v USING (cluster_id) ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Manager disk used (amber 75%, red 85%)
panels.description:
The VME manager stores its database (MySQL), OpenSearch/Elasticsearch data (logs and stats),
RabbitMQ queues, uploaded images and local backups on its disk, mostly under `/var/opt/morpheus`.

| Used | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **under 75%** | Healthy |
| **75 to 85%** | Plan: find what's growing (usually `elasticsearch`, `bitcan/backups` or `morpheus-ui/vms`) |
| **over 85%** | Act now. HPE: with the partition 85% full or more, Elasticsearch enters an unhealthy state and the appliance won't function properly. |

To free space: lower **Stats Retainment** (Administration > Settings > Appliance) or the log **Availability Time Frame**
(Administration > Settings > Monitoring), move backups to a Storage Provider, or grow the disk. HPE recommends at
least 200 GB for the manager ([requirements](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/getting_started/requirements/requirements.rst)).

This tile: the fullest filesystem on the manager. Details on the Manager & Collector dashboard.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max((f->>'percent')::numeric) FROM appliance a, jsonb_array_elements(a.health->'storage'->'files') f WHERE a.id = 1

SELECT initcap(k) AS "Service", COALESCE(a.health -> k ->> 'status', 'n/a') AS "Status" FROM appliance a, unnest(ARRAY['database', 'elastic', 'rabbit', 'cpu', 'memory', 'storage']) AS k WHERE a.id = 1
SELECT name AS "Cloud", type_name AS "Type", status AS "Status", last_sync AS "Last sync" FROM clouds WHERE present ORDER BY name
SELECT ts AS "Time", activity_type AS "Type", name AS "Object", message AS "Message", user_name AS "User" FROM activity ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Worst VM CPU ready
panels.description:
**CPU ready** is the share of time a VM's vCPUs were ready to run but had to wait for a physical core.
VME reports it per VM as the average across its vCPUs (for a host: across the VMs on it).

| Per vCPU | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **under 5%** | Healthy | Nothing |
| **5 to 10%** | Contention: VMs are queuing for CPU | Check the host's CPU usage and vCPU:core ratio; watch the trend |
| **over 10%** | VMs are noticeably slowed | Move VMs to a quieter host, cut vCPUs on oversized VMs, or add capacity |

Look at sustained values: short spikes during backups, patching or boot storms are normal.
Too many vCPUs per physical core raises ready time for every VM on the host, so right-size large VMs first.

VME added this "CPU Ready-equivalent metric" in 9.1.0; HPE doesn't document how it's calculated or a threshold. At low load it reads several times higher than the kernel's
own measurement (*vCPU wait* on the exporter dashboards), so these thresholds err on the side of warning early.
When the two disagree, trust vCPU wait.

This tile: the highest per-VM average right now.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max(v) FROM (SELECT last(m.value, m.time) AS v FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE m.time > now() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_ready_pct' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) GROUP BY m.entity_id) x

panels.title: VME CPU weight
panels.description: Each rectangle is a VM, sized and coloured by its share of the cluster's CPU. Spot the few VMs that dominate a resource at a glance. Uses VME's latest sample. Share = the VM's CPU usage × its vCPUs, divided by the cores of all hosts. Running VMs only. Very small VMs can be too thin to see; hover for values, or use the VME Data Export dashboard.

targets.rawSql: WITH cap AS (SELECT sum(s.max_cores)::float AS total FROM servers s WHERE s.kind = 'host' AND s.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster))) SELECT v.name || ' · ' || to_char(100.0 * (v.raw->'stats'->>'cpuUsage')::float / 100.0 * v.max_cores / NULLIF(cap.total, 0), 'FM990.00') || '%' AS "VM", 100.0 * (v.raw->'stats'->>'cpuUsage')::float / 100.0 * v.max_cores / NULLIF(cap.total, 0) AS share FROM servers v, cap WHERE v.kind = 'vm' AND v.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR v.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND v.power_state = 'on' AND (v.raw->'stats'->>'cpuUsage')::float > 0 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: VME memory weight (allocated)
panels.description: Each rectangle is a VM, sized and coloured by its share of the cluster's memory. Spot the few VMs that dominate a resource at a glance. Uses VME's latest sample. Share = the memory allocated to the VM divided by the memory of all hosts. VME reserves a VM's full allocation (no memory overcommit by default), so allocation is what it takes from the cluster; VME's in-guest usage figure is unreliable without a guest agent. Running VMs only. Very small VMs can be too thin to see; hover for values, or use the VME Data Export dashboard.

targets.rawSql: WITH cap AS (SELECT sum(s.max_memory)::float AS total FROM servers s WHERE s.kind = 'host' AND s.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster))) SELECT v.name || ' · ' || to_char(100.0 * v.max_memory::float / NULLIF(cap.total, 0), 'FM990.00') || '%' AS "VM", 100.0 * v.max_memory::float / NULLIF(cap.total, 0) AS share FROM servers v, cap WHERE v.kind = 'vm' AND v.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR v.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND v.power_state = 'on' AND v.max_memory > 0 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: VME disk weight
panels.description: Each rectangle is a VM, sized and coloured by its share of the cluster's storage. Spot the few VMs that dominate a resource at a glance. Uses VME's latest sample. Share = the VM's disk space in use divided by the capacity of the datastores its disks are on. Includes stopped VMs, which still occupy storage. Very small VMs can be too thin to see; hover for values, or use the VME Data Export dashboard.

targets.rawSql: WITH used_ds AS (SELECT DISTINCT (vol->'datastore'->>'id')::bigint AS id FROM servers v, jsonb_array_elements(v.raw->'volumes') vol WHERE v.kind = 'vm' AND v.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR v.cluster_id IN ($cluster))), cap AS (SELECT sum(d.capacity_bytes)::float AS total FROM datastores d JOIN used_ds USING (id) WHERE d.present) SELECT v.name || ' · ' || to_char(100.0 * (v.raw->'stats'->>'usedStorage')::float / NULLIF(cap.total, 0), 'FM990.00') || '%' AS "VM", 100.0 * (v.raw->'stats'->>'usedStorage')::float / NULLIF(cap.total, 0) AS share FROM servers v, cap WHERE v.kind = 'vm' AND v.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR v.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (v.raw->'stats'->>'usedStorage')::float > 0 ORDER BY 2 DESC

WITH top AS (SELECT m.entity_id FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg(m.value) DESC LIMIT $topn) SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(m.time, $__interval), s.name AS metric, avg(m.value) AS value FROM metrics m JOIN top USING (entity_id) JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

WITH top AS (SELECT m.entity_id FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric IN ('net_rx', 'net_tx') AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg(m.value) DESC LIMIT $topn) SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(m.time, $__interval), s.name AS metric, sum(m.value) / count(DISTINCT m.time) AS value FROM metrics m JOIN top USING (entity_id) JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric IN ('net_rx', 'net_tx') GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: VM disk size (provisioned)
panels.description: Median and average disk space provisioned per VM (all disks of all current VMs, running or not). A median well below the average means a few very large VMs.

targets.rawSql: SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.max_storage) AS "Median", avg(s.max_storage) AS "Average" FROM servers s WHERE s.kind = 'vm' AND s.present AND s.max_storage > 0 AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host))

panels.title: Idle VMs (CPU never above 5% in 24 hours)
panels.description: Running VMs whose CPU never went above 5% in the last 24 hours (VME's CPU figure, sampled every minute). VME's figure reads about 2% even for an idle VM, so the threshold sits above that. Candidates to power off, shrink or reclaim; check the list on the VME Virtual Machines dashboard first. Change IDLE_PCT / IDLE_WINDOW in tools/build_dashboards.py to redefine idle.

targets.rawSql: WITH w AS (SELECT m.entity_id, max(m.value) AS peak, avg(m.value) AS mean, count(*) AS samples FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' AND m.time > now() - INTERVAL '24 hours' AND s.present AND s.power_state = 'on' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) >= 10) SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE peak < 5) FROM w

SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(time, $__interval), CASE metric WHEN 'vms_on' THEN 'running' ELSE 'stopped' END AS metric, max(value) AS value FROM metrics WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND entity_type = 'summary' AND metric IN ('vms_on', 'vms_off') GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

SELECT COALESCE(power_state, 'unknown') AS state, count(*) FROM servers s WHERE present AND kind = 'vm' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
